Appearance:
 Shri Adit Raghuvanshi - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Anand Bhatt- G.A. for the State.

Order 
 1] They are heard.
Perused the case-diary.

2] This is the first application filed by the applic the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail as he is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.126/2025 registered at Police Station EOW, District Indore for the offence punishable under Sections 409,
420, 120-B of IPC and Sections 13(1)(b), 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.

3] The allegation against the applicant is of his involvement in the aforesaid case of embezzlement, wherein, the total amount involved is Rs.85,46,000/-, in which, according to the prosecution, the main accused was Mohit Gupta, who was posted in M.P. Gramin Bank, Jhabua, and who had withdrawn the amount from the dormant accounts and credited it into the accounts of various accused persons, including the present applicant.

4] Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the total amount NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35664 2 MCRC-46547-2025 attributed to the applicant is Rs.1,80,000/-, which was credited in his account, and without further controversy, the applicant is ready to deposit the aforesaid amount in the Trial Court, which may be subject to the final disposal of the case by the Trial Court.

sentences.text: 5] Counsel for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer, however, it is not denied that there are no criminal antecedents and the amount attributable to the applicant is Rs.1,80,000/- only.

6] Having considered the rival submissions, on perusal of the case diary, and taking note of the fact that there are no criminal antecedents and the applicant is also ready to deposit the amount, which has been wrongly credited in his account, this Court is inclined to allow the present application.

7] Thus, without reflecting anything on the merits of the case, the application filed under Section 482 of BNSS / 438 of Cr.P.C. on behalf of the applicant is hereby allowed subject to depositing a sum of Rs.1,80,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Eighty Thousand), and the said amount shall be subject to the final outcome of the case by the trial Court.
8] Accordingly, this application is allowed.

It is directed that upon applicant's or any other person on his behalf depositing a sum of Rs.1,80,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Eighty Thousand) in a fixed deposit in a nationalized bank and producing the receipt/certificate of the same before the concerned trial Court, in the event of arrest, applicant shall be released on bail, upon his executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) and furnishing one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).

The deposit receipt/certificate so produced by the applicant shall be endorsed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35664 3 MCRC-46547-2025 by the learned Judge of the lower Court to be, 'furnished towards the bail of the applicant and shall be subject to the final decision of the case by the trial Court'.
9] The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
He shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
10] M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
Certified copy as per rules.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Bahar Mukesh Sabnani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181458604/
